subject.title: [Architecture] Unify subagent token usage aggregation and budget enforcement across hybrid execution modes

question: Should OpenClaw add a core cross-runtime parent/child token-accounting and budget-enforcement contract, and which supported execution modes and user-visible budget behavior must it cover?
rationale: The issue asks for a new hierarchy, IPC/WebSocket propagation, and earlier cancellation semantics without proving a broken existing contract; choosing scope and ownership would set durable core behavior.

options.title: Require a narrow reproduction first
options.body: Ask for a current-main run that shows the fragmented recorded usage and the expected existing budget behavior before selecting an architecture.

options.title: Sponsor a core accounting contract
options.body: Define supported execution modes, lineage identifiers, persisted metrics, and cancellation semantics before implementation begins.

options.title: Keep accounting runtime-local
options.body: Retain current owner-specific reporting unless a concrete cross-runtime quota requirement is accepted as a core product contract.

recommendation.title: Require a narrow reproduction first
recommendation.body: Ask for a current-main run that shows the fragmented recorded usage and the expected existing budget behavior before selecting an architecture.

likelyOwner.reason: The available context only establishes the reporter as connected to the proposal; current code ownership could not be verified.
